proposal_not_implemented.current_operations: For integer sample A > 1, the kernel computes floor_root(A - 1), floor_root(A + 1), and one power to obtain ceil_root(A + 1).
proposal_not_implemented.candidate_operations: For A >= 2 and degree d >= 3, compute r = floor_root(A + 1) and q = r^d once. The lower endpoint is r if q < A, otherwise r - 1; the upper endpoint is r if q = A + 1, otherwise r + 1.
proposal_not_implemented.mathematical_argument_to_verify: When q < A, q <= A - 1 and (r + 1)^d > A + 1, so r is the lower floor root. Otherwise q >= A >= 2 implies r >= 2; the gap r^d - (r - 1)^d is at least 3, so (r - 1)^d <= q - 3 <= A - 2 < A - 1 < q, giving lower root r - 1. The upper endpoint follows from the definition of r. These are the same endpoints as the current kernel; no approximation tolerance is changed.
proposal_not_implemented.limits: This is a source-based optimization hypothesis, not an implemented change, a production proof or measured kernel attribution. Preserve the A <= 1 branch and all existing constructor, domain and extreme-precision behavior.
